R0191.title: AR/VR Device Security Risks
R0191.definition: Special security threats faced by Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) devices that may lead to privacy breaches, physical harm, or device hijacking.
R0191.description: AR/VR devices integrate numerous sensors (cameras, microphones, eye tracking, gesture recognition, etc.) and immersive interactions, facing unique risks: continuous user visual and auditory monitoring after device hijacking, stealing eye-tracking data to infer sensitive information (such as passwords, health conditions), tampering with reality overlay content to mislead user behavior, VR motion sickness attacks affecting physical health, minors' exposure to inappropriate content, etc. Device firmware and application ecosystem lack adequate security protections.
R0191.influence: Comprehensive user privacy leakage, biometric data stolen, physical space security threats, mental health impacts.

references.title: Security and privacy for augmented reality systems

observables: AR/VR devices keep uploading camera, microphone, and eye-tracking data outside active-use windows
Device firmware silently installs unsigned or unverified update packages
User visual or auditory streams are abnormally redirected to external servers
Immersive apps request combinations of sensor permissions in the background that exceed functional needs
Eye-tracking or gesture data flows to undeclared third-party SDKs or analytics domains
